clue.text: Arrive with young dog filled with restless desire

indicators.note: something filled has other material packed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
an itch is a restless craving to do something

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a puppy that is wriggling with eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restless desire' reads as describing the dog, but it is the piece the dog surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch up is an informal British phrasal verb for turning up somewhere, often unannounced.

clue.text: Drunk induced to follow preference

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: your pick is your choice or preference
led means persuaded or induced, as in led to believe

explanation.surface: A drinker is talked into choosing another round.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickled is informal slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is a slang synonym for intoxicated, as if steeped in alcohol like preserved vegetables.

clue.text: Sitcom and longer delights remade

indicators.note: something remade is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television comedy gets a remake that stretches out the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GOLDEN GIRLS was an American sitcom about four older women sharing a Miami house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Girls is a well-known American situation comedy from the late 1980s, an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: Hurried with fodder across street

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it, so one word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: hay is dried grass used as animal fodder
st is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A farmhand rushes to spread feed over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means done or acting with excessive speed, the same as rushed.

clue.text: Bottle, receiving a shake, mostly narrow

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for bottle holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to rock is to shake or sway

explanation.surface: A bottle is given a jolt, mostly through a narrow neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' applies only to the word for shake, which loses its final letter before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial describes a narrow, small-minded outlook concerned only with local matters, like a parish.

clue.text: Group in party back in past

indicators.note: placed in another word, so the turned party sits inside the word for past

parts.note: to go past is to go by

indicators.note: going back means the word for a party is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a crowd at a party in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is everyday British slang for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is an organised collection of people, as in a governing body or student body.

clue.text: For this reason, breaking point coming up for wild ox

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece splits the other
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nib is the point of a pen
so means therefore, for this reason

explanation.surface: A rule explains why a pen tip snapped on a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: NIB turned up is BIN, broken by SO: BI(SO)N.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a large wild bovine of North America and Europe, a kind of wild ox.

clue.text: One making spirits fade, keeping quiet? Right

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the word for fade has the word for quiet inside it

parts.note: to die away is to fade
still means quiet and calm
r is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A medium who summons ghosts is told to hush, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests ghosts, but means strong alcohol such as whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller produces whisky, gin and other strong liquor by distillation.

clue.text: Histrionic actor dons garment unusually vigorously

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts

indicators.note: unusually means in an unexpected way, so the letters are put in an unexpected order

parts.note: these eleven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overacting performer pulls on a costume with great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at something hammer and tongs is an idiom for doing it with great energy and force.

clue.text: Heavy dog sadly kept in enclosure

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the jumbled letters go within the word for enclosure

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the three letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A sluggish dog is miserably shut in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is heavy and filling, hard to digest; the word also suggests dull and weighty.

clue.text: Staying smooth in scene, artists are dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle into a new arrangement

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Performers dance on a stage set, looking perfectly composed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening pair of words; 'in' joins it to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Crease-resistant fabric keeps free of wrinkles, so garments made from it stay looking pressed and neat.

clue.text: Variable fund turning crazy

indicators.note: turning round makes the word for a fund run backwards

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A fund whose value keeps changing is going haywire.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'variable' often signals X, Y or Z, the unknowns of algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is an informal adjective for mad or eccentric, a colloquial synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Established lyric finally about tree by sea

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word's closing letter
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
the fir is a coniferous tree
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A poem's ending dwells on a tree beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places the sea after the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A confirmed habit or bachelor is a firmly settled, long-established one.

clue.text: Working out about time for knocking off

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the first word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: deducing is working out by reasoning
t is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone calculates the hour they can finish work for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like the definition but is the outer word; 'knocking off' means subtracting, not stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking off an amount, as from a price or bill, is taking it away, which is deducting.

clue.text: Member of order chosen after appeal, not hard

indicators.note: after means following, so the word for chosen is placed last
not hard means the abbreviation for hard is removed from the word

parts.note: charm is attractiveness or appeal
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the elite are the chosen few

explanation.surface: A monk is picked after an easy plea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARM loses its H to give CARM, followed by ELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmelites are friars or nuns of the Catholic Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, a religious order.

clue.text: Whisk egg in turn, making biscuit

indicators.note: to whisk is to beat and stir, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker beats eggs one after another to make cookies.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginger nut is a hard British ginger-flavoured biscuit, or cookie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a crisp, hard biscuit spiced with ginger, a British teatime favourite.

clue.text: Learner miserable without small vehicle

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the abbreviation for small is dropped from the word

parts.note: sorry can mean wretched or miserable, as in a sorry state
s is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A dejected learner driver is without a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is a large goods vehicle, the British term for a truck, so it is one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Voice belonging to forgotten orator

indicators.note: the letters belong to, and are found within, the words that follow

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A speaker long forgotten is remembered only by the sound of his voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is the highest common adult male singing voice, so it is one type of voice.

clue.text: Projected seat in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard by a listener, so the word's sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a throne is a royal seat

explanation.surface: A king's chair is put on show at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projected' looks like planned, but here it means hurled forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something projected has been hurled or cast forward, which is thrown.

clue.text: Able to reach remote targets, only securing relative gain initially

indicators.note: securing means holding inside, so the first word wraps around the rest

parts.note: lone means only or sole, as in a lone voice
a gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gun that hits distant targets helps a relative get her start.
explanation.walkthrough: Gran, short for grandmother, is a common crossword relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-range weapon or missile can hit objects a great distance away.

clue.text: Status of nobleman playing mad role

indicators.note: playing means acting about, so the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor plays a crazed lord on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl, a British peer, so it is a noble status.

clue.text: Repeat ceremony, retaining energy and pace

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the word for ceremony keeps the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
e is the symbol for energy in physics
rate means speed or pace

explanation.surface: A ceremony is rerun with the same vigour and tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The energy symbol slips in right after the first letter of the ceremony, not in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say or do something again, often for emphasis, which is to repeat it.

clue.text: Change in contractual terms

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Lawyers amend the wording of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or adjust it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Provide food and regular helpings of craft beer

indicators.note: regular helpings means portions taken at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A pub serves meals and steady pints of craft beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helpings' sounds like servings of food, but it means letters taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply meals and refreshments, especially for an event.

clue.text: Feature on area producing porcelain

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits atop the second

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A report on a region known for making fine ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain tableware, named after the country where it was first made.

clue.text: Trying to help editor, going after source with purpose

indicators.note: going after means following, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: a well is a source of water
an intention is a purpose or aim
ed is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor chases down an informant with a clear aim in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-intentioned means well and acts from good motives, aiming to be helpful.

clue.text: Stern breed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the back end, as of a ship
second meaning: to raise animals or children

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' reads as an adjective meaning strict, but here it is the noun for the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means the back part of something; as a verb it means bringing up young or livestock.

clue.text: Beam, beginning to take payment

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a ransom is a payment demanded for a captive's release

explanation.surface: Someone grins as they start to take the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a smile but is a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar or structural timber, as above a door or across a boat's stern.
